dsh-scrapling
Scrapling web scraping for dsh: JavaScript rendering, structured extraction and a background crawler
, behind one resident Python sidecar.
**A web-scraping extension for dsh: Scrapling as agent tools — JavaScript rendering, CSS/XPath extra
ction with self-healing selectors, sessions with login state, a background crawler and page Q&A.; Yo
u supply the interpreter and the browser engine; everything runs in one resident Python process.**
##  What it does
dsh ships `web_fetch` and `web_search`. The built-in `web_fetch` is deliberately honest and minimal:
a plain HTTP(S) GET with no JavaScript execution and an honest User-Agent. That is a good default —
and it means a single-page application yields only its loading shell, and there is no way to ask fo
r "just the product table". Measured on a page whose content exists only after JavaScript runs:
| Pipeline | Text obtained |

| raw HTML to text (no JS) | `SPA Shell / LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` |
| `Fetcher` (curl_cffi, still no JS

) | `SPA Shell / LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` |
| browser render (patchright) | full rendered DOM, Markdown
table, structured rows |
This package adds what the built-ins structurally cannot do:

- **Browser rendering** — JavaScript execution via patchright.
- **Structured extraction** — CSS/XPa

th selection returning data, not a wall of Markdown.
- **Self-healing selectors** — Scrapling's `ada
ptive` mode relocates an element after the site's markup changes; a selector that returns `None` aft
er a class rename returns the relocated element with `adaptive` on.
Everything runs against **one long-lived Python process**. That is not an optimisation: Scrapling's
session classes keep cookies, the browser engines keep a page pool, and `adaptive` keeps a SQLite fi
ngerprint database — a process per call would throw all of that away. Tools are registered **conditi
onally**: the plugin probes what the environment can actually do at startup and registers only what
will work, so the model never burns a turn on a tool that was guaranteed to fail. Every tool renders
its result row through the official tool-call view slot. `scrapling_answer` is the only tool that s
pends **another model call** — see The tools.
##  What it does not provide
[该节后续省略]
##  Security
- **SSRF.** Scrapling itself has no SSRF protection. This package adds a URL policy on the host side
— scheme allowlist, rejection of URLs with embedded credentials, length cap, rejection of an author
ity containing a backslash or control characters, DNS resolution with a whole-answer-set public-addr
ess check, IPv4-mapped and NAT64 addresses reclassified by their embedded IPv4 — and enforces the sc
heme, credential and address rules again on the Python side (the length cap stays with the host poli
cy, because it is a deployment setting). Outbound paths accept only `http`/`https` and reject embedd
ed credentials; `ws`/`wss` are judged by address alone in the WebSocket-handshake check. **What is j
udged is what gets sent**: the gate decides on the WHATWG-normalised form and the sidecar forwards t
hat same string, otherwise "judged A, connected to B" would be a bypass in its own right. The host-s
ide policy is enforced in one place (`SidecarClient.call`), and that one place screens every URL the
model hands over **as something to fetch** — `url`, plus crawl's `sitemapUrl` and `feedUrl` — with
one deliberate exclusion: the three offline parsers (`scrapling_extract`, `scrapling_locate`, `scrap

[长行截断]
- Known gaps, stated in the open:
- **Connection pinning** (an undici-level technique) is un
available for a non-Node transport, leaving a TOCTOU window between validation and connect. Static f
etches are covered by curl_cffi's `follow_redirects="safe"`; browser fetches by a route handler on t

he Python side.
- **NAT64 prefixes are not discovered dynamically.** The two standardized prefixes a
re covered; operator-specific ones must be declared via `nat64Prefixes`, otherwise a private IPv4 hi

dden inside IPv6 is judged as an ordinary public IPv6.
- **No port allowlist** (any port allowed by

default), matching dsh's own built-in fetch provider.
[该节后续省略]
##  Data and privacy
| Aspect | Content |
| On disk | Under the sidecar working directory (`dataDir`, default `~/.dsh-scrapling`): Scrapling's
`adaptive` fingerprint database when `adaptiveStorage: sqlite` (the default), `scrapling_download`'
s output in `downloads/`, the managed Python and Chromium installed by `setup --feature … --apply` (
`runtime/`), and the MCP entry written by `setup --mode … --apply` (`mcp/<mode>.patch.yml`). With `a
daptiveStorage: redis` the fingerprints are not written under `dataDir` at all — they go to the Redi
s at `redisUrl`, keyed `<prefix>:<registrable-domain>:<sha256(identifier)>`; that URL defaults to lo
opback, and pointing it at another machine hands this data to that machine. The crawl queue lands on
ly when `crawlCheckpointDir` is set (the upstream `Collector(crawldir=…)` writes it); an empty value
writes nothing. Login-state files go under `sessionStateDir` when it is configured. Screenshots are
handed to the host attachment service, which decides where they live. Settings values live in the h

ost settings document |
| Network | Fetches go to the URLs the model supplies, through the configure
d proxy if any. Search queries go from the Python sidecar to the single backend `searchBackend` sele
cts — Tavily (`api.tavily.com`, key in the request body), Bing (`www.bing.com`, no key), Brave (`api
.search.brave.com`, `X-Subscription-Token`), Serper (`google.serper.dev`, `X-API-KEY`), DuckDuckGo (
`html.duckduckgo.com`, no key) or the SearXNG instance at `searxngEndpoint`. A backend receives only
its own credential (`tavilyApiKey` / `braveApiKey` / `serperApiKey`) plus the query string; keys ar
e never logged. Turning on `searchPublicFallback` lets `auto` send queries to a public engine with n
o credential at all. `scrapling_answer` sends the fetched page text and the question through the hos

t `llm` service — that content leaves the machine when the routed model is remote |
| Logs | The cho
sen interpreter, the probed capabilities, and the proxy summary (`scheme://host:port` plus which run

g answered — never credentials) |
[该节后续省略]
